meta.title: TCP and TLS Handshake: What Happens Before Your First Byte

cards.title: Three Round Trips Before Data
items: TCP handshake: 1 round trip to establish a reliable connection
TLS handshake: roughly 2 more round trips (classic TLS 1.2 style) to authenticate the server and derive a session key
Only after that does the actual encrypted API request in this diagram get sent

cards.title: Two Layers, Two Jobs
items: TCP guarantees ordered, reliable delivery and detects lost packets via sequence numbers
TLS authenticates the server via its certificate and encrypts everything that follows
Neither layer needs a pre-shared secret — the handshake derives one on the fly

cards.title: Cutting the Overhead
items: TLS 1.3 collapses the handshake to 1 round trip, with 0-RTT resumption for known servers
HTTP keep-alive and connection pooling reuse a connection across many requests
HTTP/2 multiplexes many requests over one already-negotiated connection
